title: Crop Insurance Plan and Coverage Level Schedule
content:
Crop Insurance is written by the association's licensed agency with an approved insurance provider at six plan and coverage levels, from Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) through Revenue Protection 85% Coverage. The schedule below gives, for every level, the share of production and price the guarantee is built on and the price bases the guarantee uses.

## Guarantee figures by level

| Plan and coverage level | Coverage level | Price election | Revenue-based guarantee | Harvest price cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) | 50% | 55% | No | 0 (not applicable) |
| Revenue Protection 65% Coverage | 65% | 100% | Yes | 200% |
| Revenue Protection 70% Coverage | 70% | 100% | Yes | 200% |
| Revenue Protection 75% Coverage | 75% | 100% | Yes | 200% |
| Revenue Protection 80% Coverage | 80% | 100% | Yes | 200% |
| Revenue Protection 85% Coverage | 85% | 100% | Yes | 200% |

What each column means:

- **Coverage level** — Share of the approved yield (or revenue) guaranteed, %.
- **Price election** — Share of the projected price used in the guarantee, %.
- **Revenue-based guarantee** — whether the guarantee is revenue-based and rises with the harvest price.
- **Harvest price cap** — Harvest price used in the guarantee is capped at this % of the projected price; a figure of 0 means not applicable.

## Price bases by level

| Plan and coverage level | Projected price basis | Harvest price basis |
|---|---|---|
| Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) | February average of the harvest futures contract | none |
| Revenue Protection 65% Coverage | February average of the harvest futures contract | harvest-month average of the same futures contract (October for corn and soybeans) |
| Revenue Protection 70% Coverage | February average of the harvest futures contract | harvest-month average of the same futures contract (October for corn and soybeans) |
| Revenue Protection 75% Coverage | February average of the harvest futures contract | harvest-month average of the same futures contract (October for corn and soybeans) |
| Revenue Protection 80% Coverage | February average of the harvest futures contract | harvest-month average of the same futures contract (October for corn and soybeans) |
| Revenue Protection 85% Coverage | February average of the harvest futures contract | harvest-month average of the same futures contract (October for corn and soybeans) |

The projected price basis is how the projected price is set; the harvest price basis is how the harvest price is set.

## Entry requirements by level

| Plan and coverage level | Plan | Minimum years of actual production history | Sales closing deadline | Insurable interest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) | yield protection at catastrophic level | no minimum listed | March 15 | required |
| Revenue Protection 65% Coverage | revenue protection | 4 | March 15 | required |
| Revenue Protection 70% Coverage | revenue protection | 4 | March 15 | required |
| Revenue Protection 75% Coverage | revenue protection | 4 | March 15 | required |
| Revenue Protection 80% Coverage | revenue protection | 4 | March 15 | required |
| Revenue Protection 85% Coverage | revenue protection | 4 | March 15 | required |

## Notes on reading the schedule

**Which levels rise with the harvest price.** Only the five Revenue Protection levels carry a revenue-based guarantee, and only they have a harvest price basis. Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) has neither, and its harvest price cap figure of 0 marks the cap as not applicable.

**The price election at work (hypothetical figure).** Taking an illustrative projected price of $4.00 per bushel, the price used in a Catastrophic Risk Protection (CAT) guarantee is 55% of it, $2.20, while every Revenue Protection level uses 100% of it, $4.00.

**The harvest price cap at work (hypothetical figures).** With an illustrative projected price of $4.00, the harvest price used in a Revenue Protection guarantee can be no more than 200% of $4.00, that is $8.00, however high the released harvest price.
